questions.question: Mr. Robert lives in ________ Hague.
questions.explanation: "The Hague" is a proper name where "The" is part of the name itself (from Dutch "Den Haag"), not an article. So "the" is used.

questions.question: England is ________ European country.
questions.explanation: "European" begins with a vowel letter but has a consonant sound /j/ (like "you-ropean"). When vowel sounds like "iu/wa", use "a" not "an." → "a European country."

questions.question: I found ________ old lady came to our house.
questions.explanation: "Old" begins with a vowel sound /ɒ/ → use "an". → "an old lady."

questions.question: She is now a student of ________ university.
questions.explanation: "University" begins with vowel letter "u" but pronounced /juː/ (consonant sound) → use "a". → "a university."

questions.question: Iron is ______ useful metal.
questions.explanation: "Useful" begins with "u" but is pronounced /juːs/ (consonant sound) → use "a". → "a useful metal."

questions.question: Which one of the followings is in plural form?
questions.explanation: Media = plural of medium. Datum (s) → Data (p). Locus (s) → Loci (p). Radius (s) → Radii (p).

questions.question: Which is the plural form of 'Mr.'?
questions.explanation: Messrs is the formal abbreviation for the plural of Mr. (from French "Messieurs").

questions.question: Identify singular number-
questions.explanation: Formula (s) → Formulae/Formulas (p). Fungi (p) → Fungus (s). Agenda (p) → Agendum (s). Data (p) → Datum (s).

questions.question: What is the feminine gender of 'earl'?
questions.explanation: Earl (masculine) → Countess (feminine). An earl is a British nobleman; his wife/female equivalent is a countess.

questions.question: The feminine gender of the word 'bull' is-
questions.explanation: Bull (masculine) → Cow (feminine). Ewe = female sheep. Mare = female horse. Calf = young of cattle (common gender).

questions.question: What is the feminine gender of 'swain'?
questions.explanation: Swain (masculine, young man) → Nymph (feminine). Witch (feminine) → Wizard (masculine). Bitch (feminine) → Dog (masculine).

questions.question: Which one of the following is a masculine gender?
questions.explanation: Stag (masculine deer) → Hind/Doe (feminine). Buck (masculine deer). Roe (feminine deer). Vixen (feminine fox) → Fox (masculine).

questions.question: Which one is the opposite gender of doctor?
questions.explanation: Doctor is a common gender word. To specify feminine → "lady doctor." "Doctress" is not standard English.

questions.question: Which of the following is not used as a dual gender?
questions.explanation: Steward (masculine) → Stewardess (feminine) — distinct forms, not dual gender. Professor, Doctor, Cook are common/dual gender words.

questions.question: She eagerly flipped through the latest issue of ________ Time magazine to check out the upcoming fashion trends.
questions.explanation: Magazine names do NOT take "the" (unlike newspaper names). → "Time magazine" (no article).

questions.question: All he needed was ________ dollars to fuel his road trips and wandering spirit.
questions.explanation: 'A few' is used before countable nouns for a small but positive number. 'Dollar' is countable. 'A little' is for uncountable nouns.

questions.question: _____ pair of socks _____ too small for me.
questions.explanation: With 'This/A/The + pair of + plural noun', the verb must be singular. 'This pair of socks is' — the verb agrees with 'pair', not 'socks'.
